papers.title: Statistical-to-computational gaps in central limit theorems for high-dimensional tensors
papers.abstract: We study high-dimensional central limit theorems (CLTs) as hypothesis testing problems, comparing the number of summands needed for statistical and computational indistinguishability of the normalized sum from the limiting Gaussian distribution as the dimension and number of summands grow together. For the off-diagonal entries of sums of i.i.d. rank-one tensors formed from standard Gaussian vectors (equivalently, the problem of distinguishing Wigner from Wishart tensors), we prove total variation bounds sharpening previous estimates of Mikulincer (2020) and give matching polynomial-time tests. This shows that the statistical and computational thresholds coincide for this CLT, contrary to a proposal by Kunisky, Moore, and Wein (2024). On the other hand, we also show that, for tensors of order at least three, sufficient Gaussian dilution of the summands by adding independent Gaussian noise and rescaling gives a CLT model with a statistical-to-computational gap (in the above setting and ones with more general rank-one summand distributions). To the best of our knowledge, such a phenomenon has not been observed before in any high-dimensional CLT. In particular, in the relevant parameter regimes, we show that a brute-force search achieves strong detection, while polynomials of degree up to $n^{\Omega(1)}$ cannot achieve strong separation. The latter lower bounds control low-degree $\chi^2$-divergences by a novel method based on cumulant generating functions, and we further illustrate the use of these tools by applying them to masked tensor CLT models where only a prescribed subset of tensor entries is revealed.

papers.title: Sharp Lower Bounds for Parallel Log-Concave Sampling
papers.abstract: How many rounds of parallel queries are needed to sample from a smooth, strongly log-concave distribution on $\mathbb{R}^d$? For every fixed condition number $\kappa \in (1, \infty)$, we prove that any sampler making polynomially many queries per round requires $\Omega_\kappa(\log d)$ rounds to achieve constant total variation error in the worst case. The lower bound holds even if queries return derivatives of all orders. Together with the first-order parallel Picard algorithm of \cite{zhou2025parallel}, this establishes a depth complexity of $\Theta_\kappa(\log d)$ for parallel log-concave sampling with $\operatorname{poly}(d)$ width. We then study centered Gaussian targets to understand how much width is needed at a given depth. From \cite{chewi2023query,zhou2026complexitygaussiansampling}, it is known that either one round of width $d$ or $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{\kappa} \log d)$ rounds of constant width suffice for first-order Gaussian sampling. At fixed $\kappa$ we characterize the depth-width tradeoff interpolating between these regimes: when using $ \lceil c \log d\rceil$ rounds, if $0 < c < c_\star(\kappa)$ then the optimal width at constant TV error is $\widetilde{\Theta}(d^{1-c/c_\star(\kappa)})$, while if $c \geq c_\star(\kappa)$ then it is $\Theta_\kappa(1)$. Here, $c_\star(\kappa)$ is an explicit constant with $c_\star(\kappa) \sim \sqrt{\kappa} / 8$ as $\kappa \to \infty$.

papers.title: Combinatorial Bernoulli Factories with Polynomially Many Coins
papers.abstract: We provide an efficient implementation of combinatorial Bernoulli factories. Such a factory turns coins of unknown biases $x$ into a random vertex of a polytope $P$ whose mean is exactly $x$. For every affine slice of the cube (the class of polytopes that admit a factory), we give a single algorithm whose expected number of coin flips and running time at every interior $x$ are polynomial in the dimension and in $1/{\delta_*}$, where ${\delta_*}=\min_i\{x_i,1-x_i\}$ is never supplied to the algorithm. For perfect matchings this gives $O(n^{8}{\delta_*}^{-2}\log(n/{\delta_*}))$ flips, while the factory of Niazadeh, Paes Leme, and Schneider [STOC 2021] spends at least $n^{2n-1}$ flips in expectation at the uniform doubly stochastic matrix. For other polytopes, our method rounds exactly given a point deep inside $P$ and the promise that $x$ is far from the boundary of $P$.

papers.title: Nonlinear lower-tail large deviations at criticality
papers.abstract: We introduce general methods to derive lower tail large deviation principles, for a variety of nonlinear problems of combinatorial interest. These methods are especially effective in "critical" regimes, where the nonlinearities are not sparse enough for Poissonian lower tails (e.g., Janson's inequality does not provide a sharp tail bound), but the situation is not so dense that combinatorial effects dominate (e.g., we cannot directly apply the theory of hypergraph containers or the relative entropy framework of Kozma-Samotij). In particular, these are regimes where one expects interesting phase transitions to occur. Our results have a number of consequences related to subgraphs in random graphs, answering various questions of Warnke and Jenssen-Perkins-Potukuchi-Simkin. For example, consider a random graph $G\sim \mathbb G(n,p)$, and let $L_\triangle(n,p)=\log\Pr[G\text{ is triangle-free}]$. The first-order asymptotics of $L_\triangle(n,p)$ have long been known in all parameter ranges except the critical regime where $p$ has order of magnitude $1/\sqrt n$. We are able to fill this gap: for any fixed $c>0$, we show that $n^{-3/2}L_\triangle(n,c/\sqrt n)$ converges to a limit expressed in terms of a two-parameter variational problem, which has a single phase transition at $c\approx 4.341$. In contrast, we show that there is no such phase transition for the probability that $G$ is $C_{2\ell}$-free, for any fixed even cycle $C_{2\ell}$. We also obtain some applications in combinatorial design theory. Addressing conjectures of Glock-K\"uhn-Lo-Osthus, Kelly, and Kwan-Sah-Sawhney-Simkin, we obtain new estimates on the number of order-$n$ Steiner triple systems with no Pasch configuration and the number of order-$n$ Latin squares with no $2\times 2$ Latin subsquare (both tight up to a factor of $\exp(o(n^2))$).

papers.title: Functional Stochastic Localization
papers.abstract: Eldan's stochastic localization is a probabilistic construction that has proved instrumental to modern breakthroughs in high-dimensional geometry and the design of sampling algorithms. Motivated by sampling under non-Euclidean geometries and the mirror descent algorithm in optimization, we develop a functional generalization of Eldan's process that replaces Gaussian regularization with regularization by any positive integer multiple of a log-Laplace transform. We further give a mixing time bound on the Markov chain induced by our localization process, which holds if our target distribution satisfies a functional Poincar\'e inequality. Finally, we apply our framework to differentially private convex optimization in $\ell_p$ norms for $p \in [1, 2)$, where we improve state-of-the-art query complexities in a zeroth-order model.

papers.title: Discrete Isoperimetric Inequalities via Curvature
papers.abstract: Isoperimetric inequalities on the Boolean hypercube play a fundamental role in the analysis of Boolean functions. These inequalities have been established primarily for the uniform measure and for biased product measures, often through Fourier-analytic or inductive arguments. We develop a curvature-based semigroup framework to establish isoperimetric inequalities for measures with weakly dependent coordinates. In particular, we show that a Dobrushin-type condition, together with marginal boundedness of the distribution, implies the local Bobkov inequality, Talagrand's $L^1$--$L^2$ and variance--surface-area inequalities, the Kahn--Kalai--Linial inequality, and the Eldan--Gross inequality. Our results apply to zero-field Ising models with interaction matrix $J$ throughout the Dobrushin uniqueness regime $\|J\|_1<1$. The framework builds on discrete Bakry--\'Emery theory and gradient estimates and can also be extended to measures on Hamming slices or hypergrids.

papers.title: Strong error estimates for finite element approximations of the stochastic Burgers--Huxley equation with multiplicative noise
papers.abstract: This paper is concerned with strong error estimates for fully discrete finite element approximations of the stochastic Burgers--Huxley equation with multiplicative noise. We use the implicit Euler--Maruyama scheme for time discretization and continuous piecewise linear finite elements for spatial discretization. Moment bounds and exponential integrability estimates are established and used with the discrete stochastic Gronwall inequality to derive error estimates in full expectation. Sub-second-moment error estimates are first obtained in the discrete maximum-in-time $L^2$-norm and the discrete $L^2$-in-time $H^1$-norm. Second-moment error estimates in the discrete maximum-in-time $L^2$-norm are then established using a higher-moment argument. The convergence rates are of order $k^{1/2}$ in time and $h$ in space, with the spatial rate being optimal in the $H^1$-norm. Finally, numerical experiments are provided to examine the convergence rates and the influence of multiplicative noise on the solution.

papers.title: Almost sure asymptotics of numerical errors for SDEs with additive noise
papers.abstract: In this paper, we characterize the sharp almost sure asymptotics for the numerical error of the Euler--Maruyama method applied to stochastic differential equations with additive noise. Specifically, we establish, to our knowledge, the first sharp laws of the iterated logarithm for Euler--Maruyama errors in this setting along geometric mesh refinements $(N_i)_{i\in\mathbb N^+}=(\alpha^i)_{i\in\mathbb N^+}$ for any integer $\alpha\geq 2$. These results identify $(N_i)^{-1}\sqrt{\log\log N_i}$ as the sharp almost sure error scale and provide an explicit expression for the path-dependent constants governing the asymptotic error envelopes. The LIL constants also admit a natural interpretation through the asymptotic error distribution, specifically through the conditional covariance matrix of the stable limit of the rescaled error given the driving Wiener process. A central challenge in establishing these results is to characterize the almost sure fluctuations of Skorohod integrals arising in the error expansion, which are generally anticipating, non-Gaussian, and dependent across refinement levels. The analysis also provides a framework for studying analogous asymptotics for other numerical methods.

papers.title: A Finite Markov Chain Analysis of the Simplified Swarm Optimisation Update Rule
papers.abstract: Simplified swarm optimisation (SSO) updates each variable by one draw that copies the global or personal best, keeps the current value or redraws uniformly, with probabilities $c_g$, $c_p$, $c_w$ and $c_r$. As a finite Markov chain under frozen memory, its coordinate kernel $c_w I + (1 - c_w)\Pi$ has an explicit stationary law and exact convergence rate $c_w^t$. The elitist chain has a geometric hitting-time bound, from a non-optimal start a fixed $c_r$ needs at least $\exp(nc_r/2)$ expected evaluations to reach a unique optimum, and a coupling under changing memories gives $O(n\log n)$ and $O(n^2)$ expected generations on OneMax and LeadingOnes for every population size with redraw share of order $1/n$ and no inertia, and within a $\log n$ factor for fixed inertia. With a frozen memory, inertia cannot speed up first entry into any set from stationary positions, though it can from others. Where the three reference values agree, only $c_r$ acts; where they disagree, copy branches recombine the memories, forcing a redraw only where no active branch holds the target value. Branch logging and checkpoint replay show inertia slowed the tested OneMax and LeadingOnes runs and suggest memory-mediated gains on wider gaps. On Jump functions SSO needed 3.8--8.9 times fewer evaluations than the (1+1) evolutionary algorithm with rate $1/n$, but no consistent advantage over rate-adjusted mutation or a $(\mu+1)$ genetic algorithm with uniform crossover was established. The analytical redraw rule improved six of eight benchmark--setting pairs and redundancy allocation, but was slower than $c_r = 0.1$ on Jump$_2$.

papers.title: Strong Approximation of Stochastic Burgers Equations with Space-Time White Noise
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish algebraic strong convergence rates for spectral Galerkin and fully discrete approximations of the stochastic Burgers equation driven by additive space--time white noise. For deterministic initial data in $H^1$, the spectral approximation is shown to be convergent in the spatial supremum norm, uniformly in time and in every finite probability moment, with order arbitrarily close to $1/2$. Furthermore, we prove that an accelerated fully tamed exponential method possesses spatial and temporal strong convergence orders arbitrarily close to $1/2$ and $1/4$ under a CFL condition. The key to our analysis is a polynomial stability estimate for the conservative Burgers flux, which allows us to control the nonlinear error using polynomial moment bounds for the exact and numerical solutions. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first algebraic strong convergence rates on the whole probability space for this equation with additive space--time white noise.

papers.title: A Tail-Respecting Splitting Numerical Scheme for L\'evy-Driven SDEs With Superlinear Drifts
papers.abstract: We present an explicit numerical approximation scheme, denoted by $\{X^n\}$, for the effective simulation of solutions $X$ to a multivariate stochastic differential equation (SDE) with a superlinearly growing $\kappa$-dissipative drift, where $\kappa>1$, driven by a multiplicative heavy-tailed L\'evy process that has a finite $p$-th moment, with $p>0$. We show that the strong $L^{p_X}$-convergence $\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\mathbf E \|X^n_t-X_t\|^{p_X}=\mathcal O (h_n^{\gamma})$ holds for any $p_X\in (0,p+\kappa-1)$, which is exactly the range where the $p_X$-moment of the solution is known to be finite. Additionally, for any $p_X\in (0,p)$ we establish strong uniform convergence: $\mathbf E\sup_{t\in[0,T]} \|X^n_t-X_t\|^{p_X}=\mathcal{O} ( h_n^{\delta} )$. In both cases we determine the convergence rates $\gamma$ and $\delta$. In the special case of SDEs driven solely by a Brownian motion, our numerical scheme preserves super-exponential moments of the solution. The scheme $\{X^n\}$ is realized as a combination of a well-known Euler method with a Lie-Trotter type splitting technique.

papers.title: A Goal-Oriented Bayesian Experimental Design to Reduce Uncertainty in Sparse-Angle X-ray Computed Tomography
papers.abstract: Sparse-angle X-ray computed tomography (CT) presents a challenge for reliable inference, as limited measurements may leave object boundaries unresolved. Bayesian optimal experimental design (BOED) methods select informative measurements, but can be computationally expensive or require data-driven surrogates and do not explicitly exploit microlocal visibility. We address this limitation by focusing on estimating inclusion boundaries rather than the entire attenuation field. For piecewise-constant objects, these boundaries correspond to singularities characterized by their wavefront sets. Microlocal analysis determines the X-ray view-angles at which these singularities are visible. We combine this information with Bayesian uncertainty quantification to introduce B-MUSE, a microlocal uncertainty-driven sequential experimental design method. We define a microlocal C-optimality criterion associated with the wavefront direction of the most uncertain boundary singularity and prove that its optimal solution satisfies the microlocal visibility condition. B-MUSE uses this result to sequentially select informative view-angles according to boundary uncertainty. It also incorporates an adaptive stopping criterion that terminates acquisition when additional measurements provide no meaningful uncertainty reduction. We evaluate B-MUSE through numerical experiments, including interpretable examples, prior-generated inclusions, and a multi-inclusion example from an external dataset, and benchmark it against recent methods. The results show that B-MUSE substantially reduces posterior uncertainty with few adaptively selected measurements while providing boundary estimates. These findings establish a direct connection between BOED and microlocal visibility and demonstrate the potential of uncertainty-driven acquisition to reduce measurement requirements for goal-oriented X-ray CT without training data.

papers.title: An Eyring-Kramers Formula for Singular Wells
papers.abstract: Understanding the persistence of learned behaviors in AI safety motivates an investigation of the dynamical counterpart to the equilibrium geometry studied in singular learning theory. We analyze this persistence through transitions between singular wells. We establish an Eyring-Kramers formula for a low temperature Langevin diffusion between two compact connected zero components of a real-analytic potential. The wells may be singular and nonisolated, and the unique minimizing gate is a nondegenerate index-one saddle, with gates understood as inclusion-minimal sets meeting every minimizing path. A boundary-gate construction shows that uniqueness of this inclusion-minimal gate is equivalent to every minimizing path passing through the saddle and one such path meeting the communication level only there. Compact semianalytic topology provides a separating function away from a fixed saddle neighborhood; analytic Morse coordinates give matching capacity bounds by first sending the temperature to zero and then shrinking that neighborhood. An anchored energy estimate and a small-ball potential-theoretic identity give uniformity for deterministic starting points. The leading constant is expressed in terms of the sublevel-volume coefficient, a Gamma factor, and the saddle Hessian.

papers.title: Higher order convergence rate in probability for approximations of the stochastic Burgers and Cahn-Hilliard equation
papers.abstract: We consider temporal approximations of stochastic PDEs driven by additive space-time white noise, with nonlinearities that may lose both integrability and regularity. Our key examples are the stochastic Burgers equation in dimension 1 and the stochastic Cahn-Hilliard equation in dimensions $\leq 3$. We show that the accelerated exponential Euler scheme achieves a rate of convergence in probability that is well beyond the state of the art: arbitrarily close to $3/4$ in the case of Burgers and $1-d/8$ in the case of Cahn-Hilliard.

papers.title: A posteriori error estimates for fully coupled McKean-Vlasov FBSDEs with jumps
papers.abstract: We prove a two-sided a posteriori error estimate for numerical approximations of fully coupled McKean-Vlasov forward-backward SDEs with jumps under full-tuple law dependence. The coefficients may depend on the joint law of $(X,Y,Z,U)$, and we allow infinite jump activity. We construct a computable estimator ${\mathcal{E}_\pi}$ for the squared full-tuple error ${\mathcal{D}_\pi}$ relative to the exact Euler solution. The estimator uses the boundary and cumulative residuals of any admissible grid approximation. Under monotonicity and on sufficiently fine grids, $c\,{\mathcal{E}_\pi} \le {\mathcal{D}_\pi} \le C\,{\mathcal{E}_\pi}$. The efficiency bound holds without monotonicity or a mesh restriction. Analogous two-sided bounds hold for the continuous-time error up to a discretisation remainder that vanishes under coefficient time regularity. Closed-form and state-nonlinear benchmarks cover full-tuple law dependence, mark-dependent jump integrands, nonzero orthogonal martingales and infinite jump activity. In our experiments, the estimator tracks the discrete error during neural training and across Picard iterations. In a mean-field inventory model, we use the estimator and a computable discretisation term to bound the excess cost of the computed control over the discrete optimum.

papers.title: Ignoring Blow-Ups for Approximations
papers.abstract: It is well known that for SDEs with non-Lipschitz coefficients, the Euler scheme can fail to converge in an Lp sense. It is also widely observed that convergence fails only due to rare explosive trajectories, that distort the expectation. In this work we demonstrate that almost any method of removing these rare explosive trajectories leads to convergence in a suitable strong and weak sense. We apply this framework to coefficients that grow faster than linearly at infinity and Lennard-Jones type coefficients that explode like a reciprocal power on a compact set.

papers.title: Off-diagonal decay of capacitance matrices via Brownian motion
papers.abstract: We establish upper and lower bounds for the off-diagonal entries of the capacitance matrix of infinite systems of spherical resonators in chain, screen and crystal geometries. Let $d$ denote the distance between two resonator centres. For chains contained in a cylinder of bounded radius and with bounded axial gaps, the decay is of order $d^{-1}\log^{-2}(2+d)$. For screens contained in a slab and relatively dense in the tangential directions, it is of order $d^{-3}$. For relatively dense three-dimensional configurations, we obtain exponential upper and lower bounds. No periodicity is assumed. Our proofs are based on the classical connection between the Dirichlet problem and Brownian motion, which enables us to relate the decay estimates to hitting probabilities of Brownian motion.

papers.title: Sharp partition function bound for the attractive logarithmic gas
papers.abstract: For the attractive logarithmic potential, we prove that the partition function is bounded uniformly in the number of particles on every compact inverse-temperature interval $[0,\be_0]$ with $\be_0<B$, where $B\in(0,2\d]$ is the sharp constant in the logarithmic Hardy--Littlewood--Sobolev inequality. The proof separates a smooth bulk, which inherits the entropy inequality, from a short-range singular interaction. The singular contribution is controlled on the event that each box of a fixed grid contains few particles. The complementary overcrowding event has exponentially small probability, which compensates a crude linear-in-$N$ bound on the log partition function. The resulting estimate supplies the partition bound that can be used recycled in a few different results. A separate Lean formalization verifies the conditional partition-bound theorem under the log-HLS assumption.

papers.title: Uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for the Kuramoto model on the sphere
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for a generalization of the classical Kuramoto model on spheres of arbitrary dimension. For $n$ particles that are initialized independently from a probability measure with an $L^p$ density, $p>1$, and a nonzero mean vector, we obtain an explicit high-probability bound for the supremum over all times of the Wasserstein distance between the empirical and mean-field distributions. In sufficiently high dimension, this bound has the same order as the standard empirical sampling rate on the sphere and is therefore optimal. The proof combines a finite-time propagation of chaos estimate, a quantitative synchronization result for the mean-field model, and a late-time stability estimate of the system.

papers.title: Gaussian fluctuations and moderate deviations for two-dimensional stochastic nematic liquid crystal flows
papers.abstract: We study the small-noise behaviour of a two-dimensional stochastic nematic liquid crystal model, where the Navier--Stokes equations with multiplicative noise are coupled with a Ginzburg--Landau equation for the director field driven by geometric Stratonovich noise. While large deviations for stochastic nematic liquid crystal models have been studied earlier, the central limit and moderate deviation regimes have not been considered. We first prove a central limit theorem in the natural energy space and show that the rescaled fluctuations converge, in every $L^p$-norm and with rate $\sqrt{\eps}$, to the solution of a linear stochastic system. The limiting process is centred Gaussian. We then establish a moderate deviation principle with a quadratic rate function determined by the corresponding linearised skeleton equation, which coincides with the Cameron--Martin form of the Gaussian limit. We also show that the moderate deviation principle holds uniformly over bounded sets of initial data. The main arguments use a cancellation between the coupling terms, a one-sided estimate for the polynomial potential, and energy estimates with deterministic Gronwall coefficients, thereby avoiding exponential moment estimates.

papers.title: Parabolic stochastic quantisation of the fractional $\Phi^4_3$ model in the full subcritical regime
papers.abstract: We present a construction of the measure of the fractional $\Phi^4$ Euclidean quantum field theory on $\mathbb{R}^3$ in the full subcritical regime via parabolic stochastic quantisation. Our approach is based on a truncated flow equation for the effective description of the model at sufficiently small scales and on coercive estimates for the nonlinear stochastic partial differential equation describing the interacting field. The constructed measure is translation invariant, reflection positive, and has quartic exponential tails.

papers.title: Heat kernel estimates for Markov processes with blowing-up jump kernels
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish sharp two-sided heat kernel estimates for a large class of purely discontinuous symmetric Markov processes on closed subsets $F$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$, whose jump kernels blow up on a Borel subset $\Sigma$ of $F$. We assume that $F\setminus \Sigma$ is a $\kappa$-fat set and is dense in $F$, and additionally, in case of unbounded $F$, that the Assouad dimension of $F$ is strictly less than $d$. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work establishing sharp two-sided heat kernel estimates for jump processes whose jump kernels blow up on part of the state space. The jump kernels under consideration take the form $J(x,y)=|x-y|^{-d-\alpha}{\mathcal B}(x,y)$, where $\alpha\in (0,2)$ and the function ${\mathcal B}(x,y)$ blows up at a subset $\Sigma$ of $F$. A fundamental obstacle is that the tails of the jump measures are not uniformly bounded, and hence standard techniques in heat kernel analysis do not provide a priori off-diagonal estimates. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a new approach based on weighted integral estimates for the heat kernel that are sensitive to both the blow-up behavior of the jump kernel and the geometry of $F\setminus \Sigma$. Examples of processes falling within our general framework include traces of isotropic $\alpha$-stable processes in some unbounded $C^{1,\rm Dini}$ sets, processes in Lipschitz sets arising in connection with the nonlocal Neumann problem, and a large class of resurrected self-similar processes in the closed upper half-space.

papers.title: Averaging Dynamics and Wong-Zakai approximations for a Fast-Slow Navier-Stokes System Driven by fractional Brownian Motion
papers.abstract: We study a Fast-Slow system of coupled two- and three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations in which the fast component is perturbed by an additive fractional Brownian noise with Hurst parameter $\H>\frac{1}{3}$. Using rough path theory, we establish subsequential convergence in law of the slow component, with limiting dynamics depending on the Hurst parameter and the noise scaling. For $\H<\frac12$, an averaging regime yields a deterministic Navier-Stokes equation with an additional It\^o-Stokes drift. Under a stronger noise scaling, corresponding to a Wong-Zakai approximation, and a centering condition on the quadratic fast dynamics, we obtain a Navier-Stokes equation driven by fractional transport noise. For $\H>\frac12$, the transport-noise limit holds in the Wong-Zakai regime without this centering condition, with integration understood in the Young sense.

papers.title: Non-local SDEs, critical drifts and local blow-ups
papers.abstract: The paper is concerned with $\alpha$-stable SDEs with singular time-inhomogeneous general drift. Our drifts satisfy e.g.\,a close to minimal possible critical Morrey class condition that covers local blow-ups of the type arising in some particle systems with strong attracting interactions. We develop detailed Sobolev regularity theory for the forward and backward equations, construct Feller propagator and prove weak existence and conditional uniqueness for the $\alpha$-stable SDE.

papers.title: Logarithmic derivatives of variational and singular stochastic partial differential equations
papers.abstract: For a stochastic partial differential equation posed on a Gelfand triple and satisfying the fully local monotone conditions of R\"ockner, Shang and Zhang, we compute the logarithmic derivative of the law of the solution at a fixed time along a prescribed direction of the state space. The formula is intrinsic, expressed through the Hilbert-Schmidt Malliavin derivative $\Phi_r = \mathcal{D}_r X(t)$ and the covariance $\gamma_t = \int_0^t \Phi_r \Phi_r^{*}\,\mathrm{d}r$ alone, so that neither the inversion of the first variation nor uniform Malliavin-Sobolev bounds on the Tikhonov family are needed. It follows from an integration-by-parts identity on a Hilbert space, a Moore-Penrose covering field on Wiener space and a trace formula for the Tikhonov limit, brought to the equation by the representation $\Phi_r = Y(t,r)\mathcal{B}(r,X(r))$. The linearised theory is carried by $\Phi$ and by its own Malliavin derivative $\mathcal{W} = \mathcal{D}\Phi$, whose regularity is measured in the time-integrated quadratic energy that the dissipative structure of the linearisation produces, so that no operator norm of the first variation between the spaces of the triple occurs. The stochastic $p$-Laplacian and the two-dimensional Navier-Stokes equation are treated in detail; for the latter the dissipative, forcing and exponential-moment hypotheses are established together under trace-class additive noise and a smallness threshold on the noise covariance. A scalar reduction carries the identity beyond the variational class, to the law of a pairing $\langle u(t), \varphi\rangle$ for the singular equations of Bruned, Chandra, Chevyrev and Hairer, on the same H\"older triangle of moment exponents.

papers.title: Randomly growing uniform hypergraphs
papers.abstract: We investigate growing uniform random hypergraphs whose hyperedges are $(k-1)$-simplices. At each step, one of two processes occurs: (i) a new vertex is added with probability $p$; (ii) a simplex $\langle v_1,\ldots,v_k\rangle$ with randomly chosen distinct vertices is added with probability $1-p$. Emerging random uniform hypergraphs exhibit a percolation transition. A giant component is formed when $p<p_c=1-(2k-1)^{-2}$. The fraction of vertices in the giant component scales as $\exp[-C/\sqrt{p_c-p}]$, a signature of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless phase transition. In the non-percolating phase, the cluster size distribution has an algebraic tail with a continuously varying exponent, while at $p=p_c$, it acquires a logarithmic correction. We analyze triadic hypergraphs ($k=3$) in detail and then generalize to higher $k$. We show that the Euler characteristic and the first Betti number of the giant component scale linearly with system size. Higher Betti numbers fluctuate between realizations but remain finite, and hence the normalized Euler characteristic and the first Betti number of the giant component are asymptotically equal, up to a sign.

papers.title: Sharp constants and martingale proofs for two-weight Hardy inequalities with general measures
papers.abstract: We study the least constant $C_*$ in the two-weight Hardy inequality from $L^p(\sigma)$ to $L^q(\omega)$ for the operator $H_\sigma g(x)=\int_{(0,x]}g\,d\sigma$, where $\sigma$ is a Borel measure on the half-line that is finite on each interval $(0,x]$ and $\omega$ is a $\sigma$-finite Borel measure there, atoms allowed. Let $\mathcal A$ be the Maz'ya--Rozin functional and let $1<p<\infty$. For $0<q<p$ we find the best factor $\kappa_{p,q}$ in $C_*\le\kappa_{p,q}\mathcal A$. For $1\le q<p$ we prove $C_*\ge\mathcal B\ge\mathcal A$, where $\mathcal B$ is a Lebesgue--Stieltjes form of $\mathcal A$. The factor $1$ is best possible. For $0<q<1$ we give a lower factor valid for all such measures and an upper bound for the best lower factor. This bound comes from atoms of $\omega$. It is smaller than the lower factor proved by Sinnamon (1991) for weights. A two-atom example shows that the bound is not always sharp. The proofs use a reverse martingale with Doob's inequality, a special function of Os\k{e}kowski (2015), a quantile coupling and a splitting of atoms. The same tools recover the theorem of Li and Mao (2020) for $1<p\le q$, in the closed-interval form of Klaassen and Wellner (2021). They also recover the two-sided estimate of Sinnamon and Stepanov (1996) for $0<q<p$, which goes back to Maz'ya (1979) for $q\ge1$ and to Sinnamon (1991) for $q<1$. We also treat the case $p=1$ and a discrete criterion.

papers.title: The External Path Length and Terminal Wiener Index in Random Trees
papers.abstract: We consider two distance-based concepts in rooted trees and compare them to their leaf-restricted counterparts. The path length is the sum of all distances from the root to the vertices of the tree, while the external path length is the sum of all distances from the root to the leaves of the tree. Upon dividing by the number of vertices and leaves respectively, we obtain the average distance to the root. The Wiener index is the sum of all distances between pairs of vertices, and the terminal Wiener index is the sum of all distances between pairs of leaves. Dividing by the number of pairs of vertices and pairs of leaves respectively, we obtain the average distance between vertices and average distance between leaves. For two important classes of random trees, we show that the average distance of the root to a random leaf is almost the same as the average distance to a random vertex and that the average distance between vertices is almost the same as the average distance between leaves. For Bienaym\'e--Galton--Watson trees, each of these differences is bounded in probability. For three varieties of increasing trees (recursive trees, $d$-ary increasing trees, generalised plane-oriented recursive trees), on the other hand, the differences converge to constants in probability. This allows the transfer of convergence results for the path length to the external path length, and results for the Wiener index to be transferred to the terminal Wiener index.

papers.title: Hausdorff measures of planar Brownian level sets
papers.abstract: For any Hausdorff gauge \(h\), we prove that all level sets of planar Brownian motion have zero \(h\)-measure almost surely if and only if \(\liminf_{r\to0^+}h(r)\log(1/r)=0\). This resolves Taylor's question for arbitrary Hausdorff gauges. The proof yields \(0<\HH^{h_0}(L_x)<\infty\) for some \(x\) almost surely, where \(h_0(r)=1/\log(1/r)\). The Hausdorff dimensions of the spatial mass superlevel sets form a deterministic, strictly decreasing bi-Lipschitz spectrum. For each fixed positive mass below the supremum, the exact-mass set almost surely has the same dimension as the corresponding superlevel set.

papers.title: On $L^p$ density of self-similar measures and Bernoulli convolutions
papers.abstract: We prove that an absolutely continuous self-similar measure has an $L^p$ density for some $p>1$. Moreover, explicit examples of Bernoulli convolutions with a continuous density are established.
